assessment: Two of the five defect families turned out to be one mechanism, and that is the finding: it narrows the ask Andrew is holding instead of widening it. Replaying this build's 897-record run log against windows() and beats_for() reproduces BOTH strips cell by cell, and the three false misses on harvest_intraday are owed by exactly the three runs that harvested ZERO rows. Those runs do no work and finish about 37 seconds past their slot; the six productive runs take 69-87 seconds and finish 73-91 seconds past theirs. The cell edges sit at 73 seconds past the half hour because they are anchored on generated_at (13:01:13), so this build's offset falls BETWEEN the two modes of a run-duration distribution that yield itself determines, and the two populations bin in opposite directions across one edge -- which is the whole of today's alternating ok/miss/ok/miss strip, and which finally explains the build-to-build variance in the false-red count that ten-plus events have chased without a mechanism. harvest_premarket shows both signs inside one build: its productive 08:01:31 run skips its cell forward, its zero-row 08:30:44 run collides backward, and its 07:00:39 run is deleted outright by the left-edge mask. The consequence for Andrew is the one that matters and it is not a new ask: clause (a) of the standing four -- floor the cell grid to the schedule instead of the build clock -- removes the dependence on the sub-minute offset AND on the duration distribution at once, so the ask stays at four clauses and no fifth is proposed. Said against this lane, twice: the stronger reading of this fire was that steps.run_sessions.rows == 0 is the idle-versus-broken discriminator the open residual has been waiting for, and it is FALSE -- every one of the 618 zero-row runs has run_sessions 0, but 22 runs have run_sessions 0 while harvesting 14,441 to 36,720 rows, so the implication runs one way only and e-000228's residual stays open and stays Andrew's; and the duration mechanism above holds cleanly today (13.6-17.8 s against 38.5-44.8 s, no overlap) but NOT across the month (5.2-21.4 s against 7.0-57.2 s, overlapping), so it is a property of this build's offset, not a law. One correction to this lane's own headline of 0.83 h ago: harvest_intraday now publishes rows_added_last 7,626, the first non-zero figure this lane has read on a card, so the structural blind spot stands while the instance that illustrated it has cleared on the irreversible job -- premarket and evening still publish 0 beside healthy. Nothing else moved: trunk 1a05afa for 21.5 days, zero events, tasks, bus messages or inbox lines by anyone but this lane, no receipt owed an event, the courier alive on a thirteenth direct reading and the executor leg still dead behind Andrew's merge.

items.title: The beat-grid defect and the zero-yield runs are ONE mechanism, and clause (a) alone fixes both -- the ask does not grow to five clauses
items.why: For four days this lane has reported the grid family and, since 0.83 h ago, the yield family as separate asks, and the honest reading now is that they intersect. Cells are anchored on generated_at (windows(), line 242: t0 - cad*(i+1) .. t0 - cad*i, left-closed right-open at beats_for line 254), so this build's edges sit 73 s past the half hour. A zero-row run completes all five data steps at 0 rows in about 34 s and finishes 37-39 s past its slot, short of the edge, colliding into the preceding cell and leaving its own empty -- published 'miss'. A productive run takes 69-87 s and clears the edge. Reproduced cell by cell: harvest_intraday's nine runs give ok(16) ok(17) MISS(18) ok(19) MISS(20) ok(21) MISS(22) ok(23) against the published 16 na / 5 ok / 3 miss, an exact match, and the three misses are owed by the 10:00:38, 11:00:37 and 12:00:38 runs -- all three zero-row. harvest_premarket's four runs give na(11) ok(12) MISS(13) ok(14) MISS(15), also exact, and carry BOTH signs: the productive 08:01:31 run (87.4 s) skips its cell forward, the zero-row 08:30:44 run (38.7 s) collides backward, and the 07:00:39 run lands in a cell in_schedule() masks and is deleted outright. This matters to the end goal because it changes what Andrew is deciding: the false-red count has looked like unexplained build-to-build noise across ten-plus events, and it is a deterministic function of where the build minute's sub-minute offset falls in a bimodal, yield-determined duration distribution. Flooring the grid to the schedule removes both dependencies at once. The ask therefore stays at FOUR clauses (c-0022.1 / c-0023.1) and this item proposes no fifth.
items.acceptance: Someone who was not here re-runs the replay: load data/results/run_history.jsonl, filter mode=='intraday' and mode=='premarket' to 2026-10-02, bin each record's finished_at into windows(job, t0=2026-10-02T13:01:13-05:00, 24) with the cadence from data/build/manifest.yaml, and confirm the resulting ok/miss/na sequences equal the beats arrays published in data/results/build_status.json for both jobs. Then confirm that every intraday cell published 'miss' is a cell whose own slot's run has rows==0, and that every such run's total duration (sum of steps[].seconds) is under the build's sub-minute offset of 73 s while every productive run's exceeds it. The claim is refuted if any published cell disagrees with the replay, or if a 'miss' cell is owed by a run with rows>0.

So emit already honours rules.md rev 16 row 4 for ABSENT input, and the single failed run in all 897 records (2026-09-13T09:30:04-05:00, weekend, all five steps failed, rows null) renders correctly as 'error' with a dash. This is the end-goal consequence: charter criterion 1 rests on a cache the irreversible job fills, and a job that keeps running on time and fills nothing advances no clock the monitor watches.
